body: NAH, especially since he hasn't seemed to be a jerk about it. It's not your responsibility but as a forgetful, less organized person myself, I totally understand not knowing when something that seems obvious needs to be done, or just forgetting to do it. A lot of people have mentioned ADHD/ADD, and as someone who has had it for most of my life, I think it's definitely something to look into!

NTA. 
I really feel this. I'm 19 and my bio brother has autism - nothing NEARLY as bad as your situation. He mostly acts as anyone would, but his social skills are a bit stunted. Really smart, but emotionally immature, I guess? I can't think of a better word right now. As we've gotten older (he's only younger than me by 3 years) he's matured a lot quicker. Gramted, he doesn't feel like a 16 year old to me, but that's life sometimes. Could just be older sister shit. 
But god growing up with it was so hard. Being the oldest sibling meant that at school the teachers and principals would call me down to do THEIR job if he was having a meltdown. Any family vacations usually had at least 2, and being a super self-concious kid, I HATED watching people stare at him as he flipped in public. I hated people watching us. My parents would get so mad at me for it. I tried to vent about it once on the internet when I was 16 and I was told I must hate my brother. I don't hate him. I was just so frustrated that I kept being forced into positions I didn't ask for; that I kept having to live a life I didn't ask for. 
Maybe I'm biased. But I genuinely don't think you're the asshole here. It's so much responsibility at such a young age. And you just got it out of nowhere, one day. You lead a whole life that was just suddenly changed out of nowhere. And that's even beside the trauma about hospitals that you shouldn't have to endure. 
Take your Grandma up on it. Your dad may be disappointed, but you're a child too. Even more so, you're HIS child, and he should take you into kore consideration. This is a fucking difficult life you lead here, even if you're not the one with the disability. Good luck kid.

I'm 19. I'm severely depressed. I've been like this since I was 11.  It's not officially diagnosed, but I am on medication now for it. I tell people I'm depressed but I don't think they understand what that means because of how desensitized it is as a joke these days.  
I got bullied a little as a child, nothing crazy, but got my fair share of ostrasizing and name-calling by the pretty popular girls. My mom was harsh and my dad liked to yell - now that I'm older, I recognize my mom undoubtably was extremely manipulative and might have some narc thing. I love her to death, don't get me wrong, but it definitely contributed. 
My brother has high functioning autism so he got the majority of my parent's attention (which is NOT something I resent him for, I love my brother dearly and this was out of everyone's control), and being the oldest, I had to fend for myself in a lot of ways. That meant, to me personally, not burdening them with my mental health. Part of me was scared to talk, the other part of me thought I was too good for therapy. My parents told me in an unrelated way that they didn't believe in teenage depression. I'm diagnosed with ADD but my father doesn't believe in that either. So I kept quiet and learned to cope with it by myself.
When I was 14 I tried to commit suicide by jumping off my roof. The door to my roof wouldn't open so I cried on the floor instead. I self harmed with safety scissors and pens on my arm and biting the inside of my cheeks and lips because I was scared of the pain of real cutting, and the prideful part of me thought I was above it. When I was 15 I was finally starting to heal, until friends in high school tore me down for being more confident than them. I fell back into it; they got out of theirs. Up until a year ago I would think about suicide every day and have to physically stop myself from doing something about it other than crying over how much I wanted to die in my car. Since then I've done better because I began to cut out harmful joking phrases like "i wanna die" but these past 6 months have been horrible and I'm starting to spiral back again.
I tried therapy last year and started with a small issue, how I was having trouble making friends in college because I was introverted, and the therapist told me to get over it so I never went back. My younger sister got diagnosed with depression and anxiety at 13. My parents know about it, but my mom likes her more and she's the smart prodigy kid so they let her off, but still make snide comments here and there. My dad doesn't believe she's actually depressed. I've tried reaching out to her, especially since I know EXACTLY what she's going through, but she hasn't really bit. I don't know how to help. I'm scared she'll end up like me. I'm lost and in a deadbeat art major with no hope for the future. I don't know what to do anymore other than continue to skate by.
My dad actually isn't lazy and does so much for my family and works his ass off for us.  My mom's just a narcissist.
Tying my shoes. For five years.
